def.brief: README Versioning: the **major** rule names only a changed artifact/lock/record shape. Add that dropping a supported Python or host version (a raised engines floor) is major too, and say what that means for this checkout: the >=3.11 floor (adopted in 7db34a2; the released 1.19.3 declared >=3.9 in plugin.json and .claude-plugin/plugin.json) drops 3.9 and 3.10, so it ships as part of the planned 2.0, not as a patch, and the source manifests and marketplace entries stay 1.19.3 until that coordinated release. Release and adoption's 'Documentation and shared instruction edits also need a patch bump' must not read as patch-only when the same release raises a floor. Checks: the section says it; every version field is still 1.19.3 and every python floor >=3.11 (nothing bumped); README/AGENTS/skill links and anchors resolve; git diff --check. Engine and property suites are not rerun: nothing they test changes.
checks: import json,re,sys; s=open('README.md',encoding='utf-8').read(); sec=s.split('## Versioning',1)[1].split('\n## ',1)[0]; v=[json.load(open(p))['version'] for p in ('plugin.json','.claude-plugin/plugin.json','.codex-plugin/plugin.json')]; m=json.load(open('.claude-plugin/marketplace.json')); v+=[m['metadata']['version']]+[p['version'] for p in m['plugins'] if p['name']=='mangsang']; flo=[json.load(open(p))['engines']['python'] for p in ('plugin.json','.claude-plugin/plugin.json','.codex-plugin/plugin.json')]; ok=all(w in sec for w in ('Python or host version','3.9','3.10','2.0','1.19.3')) and set(v)=={'1.19.3'} and set(flo)=={'>=3.11'}; print(v, flo, 'versioning states the floor as major' if ok else 'NOT stated / versions moved'); sys.exit(not ok)
